reason: The text portrays Yahweh as enforcing a covenant relationship through conditional judgment and reward, not as inherently antagonistic. While severe consequences for disobedience are described (judgment on Jeroboam's house, eventual scattering of Israel), these are presented as responsive to specific acts of idolatry and covenant-breaking—not as arbitrary hostility. Conversely, Yahweh offers kingdoms to those who obey, prevents civil war between Israel's divisions by commanding Rehoboam not to fight his brethren ('Do not go up or fight against your brothers...for this thing is from Me'), and makes conditional promises of blessing ('If you listen to all that I command you and walk in my ways and do what is right in my sight, then I will build you a lasting dynasty'). The overarching structure is covenantal—reward for obedience, judgment for disobedience—not antagonism.
